Blunt and Mrs Jones want somebody near the man: Drevin is one of the richest people alive, made his money in the chaotic years after the Soviet collapse, owns an English football club, and is now building Ark Angel, the first hotel in orbit, a project that has consumed more money than anyone can account for. Alex becomes a friend to Paul, who has no others, and Smithers equips him for a trip to the family's Caribbean island. What MI6 do not say is how much of their interest is in the American investigation quietly circling Drevin's finances.

On Flamingo Bay, Alex finds a private island with its own launch complex and a workforce that does not discuss its employer. Among the staff is Tamara Knight, a young woman who takes an unexplained interest in him. Force Three strikes at the island, and Alex meets its leader, Kaspar, whose head and face are covered in tattooed foliage and who talks about the planet in the language of a man for whom individual deaths do not count. The attacks are savage and the security response is oddly calm. Alex begins to notice that Force Three appears exactly where it is most useful, and that Drevin's disasters are always insured.

The pieces fit together and give Alex a different picture. Ark Angel has bankrupted its owner; Drevin's fortune was built on money and methods that will not survive examination; and the authorities are closing on him. Force Three is not his enemy but his creation, funded and directed by him to provide a public villain and a reason for everything that has gone wrong. Kaspar is a paid man who does not fully understand whose plan he is serving. Alex works out that Drevin has one move left that would solve the problem permanently, and that it involves the station currently in orbit above them.

Drevin intends to bring Ark Angel down out of orbit onto Washington, DC, destroying the buildings that hold the case against him and a great part of the city with them, and leaving the catastrophe to be blamed on the terrorists he has spent a year inventing. It cannot be stopped from the ground once it is set running. Alex is put aboard a launch bound for the station, and Tamara Knight goes with him; she is a CIA officer who has been working inside Drevin's organisation, and Alex is no longer working alone. Neither of them has flown before, the station is unmanned, and the de-orbit sequence is already loaded.

Aboard Ark Angel, Alex and Tamara Knight change the station's course so that it comes down over open ocean and breaks up there instead of over Washington; the city is never hit and the scheme is destroyed with the station. Drevin is killed, Kaspar does not survive, and his fraud and his invented terrorists are both exposed, leaving Paul orphaned and his father's name ruined. Alex is left with the problem of getting home from orbit, and solves it by falling: he comes down through the atmosphere and into the sea off the Australian coast, where he is found alive. He has been shot, told to rest for months, kidnapped, and put into space, and MI6 have still not given any indication that they are finished with him.

characters.description: A wealthy English gentleman whose life in London follows a precise and solitary routine. His calm manner, mathematical habits, and refusal to hurry make his sudden commitment to circle the world in eighty days seem all the more extraordinary.
characters.name: Phileas Fogg

characters.description: Fogg's newly hired French servant, a former acrobat and fireman who hoped that his master's strict routine would provide a quiet life. Warm, impulsive, and resourceful, he is dismayed when his first day of service turns into an immediate journey around the globe.
characters.name: Passepartout

characters.description: A member of Fogg's circle at the Reform Club. His skepticism about the practical speed of modern travel helps turn a discussion of a newspaper timetable into Fogg's twenty-thousand-pound wager.
characters.name: Andrew Stuart

characters.description: A British detective stationed at Suez, watching for the perpetrator of a recent Bank of England robbery. Fogg's abrupt departure and resemblance to the police description convince Fix that he has found his suspect, though he lacks the warrant needed to arrest him abroad.
characters.name: Fix

characters.description: A British army officer traveling across India who shares part of Fogg's route. Familiar with the country and its railway, he becomes an ally when an interruption in the journey requires the travelers to improvise.
characters.name: Sir Francis Cromarty

characters.description: A young Indian widow of Parsi background whom Fogg's party finds in grave danger during the overland journey. Educated in the European manner and without safe family protection nearby, she accepts the travelers' help in leaving India.
characters.name: Aouda

characters.description: The skilled master of the small trading vessel Tankadere. Fogg hires him when the regular steamer connection has been missed, and his seamanship gives the travelers another chance to intercept their eastward route.
characters.name: John Bunsby

characters.description: A forceful American encountered amid political disorder in San Francisco. A collision with Fogg creates a personal quarrel that neither man considers settled when they later meet again on the transcontinental railway.
characters.name: Stamp Proctor

characters.description: An American who owns a wind-driven sledge equipped to cross the frozen plains. He offers Fogg an unconventional way to continue east after the railway journey is interrupted.
characters.name: Mudge

characters.description: The stubborn master and owner of the Henrietta. He initially refuses to take Fogg directly to England, forcing a negotiation over passage aboard his Atlantic steamer.
characters.name: Andrew Speedy

recaps.ending: Fogg reaches London believing that delays and Fix's mistaken arrest have cost him the wager. Having spent much of his fortune and withdrawn from public view, he nevertheless offers to marry Aouda after she declares her love for him. When Passepartout visits a clergyman to arrange the ceremony, he discovers that the date is Saturday rather than Sunday. By traveling eastward around the globe, the party crossed the international date line and gained a calendar day without realizing it. Passepartout races back with the news, and Fogg reaches the Reform Club seconds before the agreed deadline, winning the wager. His travel costs leave little financial profit, which he shares with Passepartout and Fix, but the journey has brought Aouda into his life. Fogg and Aouda marry, making their relationship - not the money - the lasting result of the voyage.
recaps.in_short: Phileas Fogg wagers members of London's Reform Club that new transport links make it possible to circle the world in eighty days. He leaves at once with his French servant Passepartout. Detective Fix mistakes him for a bank robber and follows while awaiting a warrant. In India, Fogg sacrifices time to rescue Aouda, who then travels with the party. Missed ships, storms, Passepartout's separation, a railway attack in America, and an improvised Atlantic crossing repeatedly consume their margin. Fix finally arrests Fogg in Liverpool, only to release him when the real robber is identified. Fogg reaches London believing he is late and ruined. After Aouda proposes that they marry, Passepartout learns that eastward travel across the date line has gained them a day. Fogg arrives at the Reform Club just before the deadline and wins. He gains little money after expenses, but marries Aouda.

recaps.text: Phileas Fogg is a wealthy but enigmatic London gentleman who organizes every day with exact precision. He dismisses a servant for a small error and hires Passepartout, a Frenchman pleased by the prospect of a quiet post. That evening at the Reform Club, a discussion about a recent bank robbery turns to a newspaper calculation that the world can now be circled in eighty days. Fogg insists that the timetable is practical and wagers twenty thousand pounds with five club members that he can prove it. He must return to the club by the appointed evening eighty days later. Without making preparations beyond taking a travel bag and half the money in cash, he summons the astonished Passepartout and departs for the Continent that same night.

News of the wager spreads through Britain, where public opinion follows Fogg's progress and speculates about his chances. At Suez, Detective Fix is waiting for a suspected Bank of England robber. Fogg's appearance, large supply of cash, and hasty departure fit the police description closely enough to convince Fix that he is the fugitive. Passepartout innocently tells the detective about their route and the wager. Fix requests an arrest warrant and boards the same steamer, intending to keep Fogg within reach until legal authority catches up. Fogg remains absorbed in his timetable as the party crosses the Red Sea and Indian Ocean. In Bombay, Passepartout enters a temple without understanding the rules, is driven out by priests, and escapes without telling his master that the incident may have consequences.

The railway across India proves unfinished. Fogg buys an elephant and hires a guide to cover the missing section, accompanied by Sir Francis Cromarty. In the forest they learn that Aouda, a young widow, is to be killed in a coerced funeral rite. Fogg decides that their schedule allows time for a rescue. After an initial plan fails, Passepartout takes the place of the dead husband on the funeral structure and carries Aouda away when the crowd believes a miracle has occurred. The travelers reach the railway and continue to Calcutta. There, Fogg and Passepartout are arrested over the Bombay temple incident. Fogg pays bail rather than lose the departing steamer. Sir Francis leaves them, while Aouda, unable to find safety with her relatives in India, continues toward Hong Kong under Fogg's protection. Fix follows, still waiting for his warrant.

Fix tries to delay Fogg before he leaves British territory, but the warrant still does not arrive. At Hong Kong, Aouda learns that the relative she hoped to join has moved away, and Fogg calmly offers to take her onward to Europe. The next steamer's departure is advanced. Fix tells Passepartout that he is a detective and, when the servant refuses to help, leaves him drugged and unable to warn Fogg. Fogg and Aouda miss the ship and believe Passepartout has gone ahead alone. Fogg hires Captain John Bunsby and the Tankadere to catch another connection near Shanghai. Meanwhile Passepartout reaches Yokohama aboard the scheduled steamer without money or companions. He survives by joining an acrobatic troupe. Fogg, Aouda, and Fix arrive in Yokohama by another route, and Fogg recognizes Passepartout during a performance. Reunited, the party boards a steamer for San Francisco, with Fix now intending to help Fogg reach England before making an arrest there.

In San Francisco, Fogg and Fix are caught in a violent political gathering, where Fogg quarrels with Colonel Stamp Proctor. The travelers then take the transcontinental railway. Their route includes a precarious crossing, an encounter with a Mormon speaker, and the return of Proctor, but a larger danger interrupts the men's planned duel: an attack on the train. Passepartout helps separate the engine from the carriages and is carried away with other captives. Although abandoning him threatens the schedule, Fogg leads soldiers back to rescue him. They succeed, but the train has gone. Fix secures a wind-powered sledge driven by Mudge, enabling Fogg, Aouda, and Passepartout to cross the frozen plains and regain an eastbound connection. They reach New York only after the Liverpool steamer has departed.

Fogg charters the Henrietta from Captain Speedy on the understanding that it will take the party toward Europe. Once at sea, he redirects the ship toward Liverpool. When fuel runs low, he buys the vessel and burns its wooden fittings to keep the engines running, finally landing in Britain with almost no margin left. Fix immediately arrests him. After a damaging delay, the detective learns that the actual bank robber has already been caught and releases Fogg. Fogg strikes Fix in anger and makes a final dash by special train and hired carriage, but reaches London after the deadline he has calculated. Convinced that the wager is lost, he returns home with Aouda and Passepartout. His remaining funds are committed to his obligations, and he withdraws in apparent ruin.

Believing himself defeated, Fogg remains composed and offers to provide what little security he can for Aouda. She declares her love and asks him to marry her; he gladly agrees. Passepartout goes to arrange the ceremony and discovers that the party has mistaken the day. Because they traveled eastward and crossed the international date line, they experienced one fewer sunrise than people in London and have gained a full calendar day. Passepartout rushes home, and Fogg races to the Reform Club. He enters only seconds before the original deadline and wins the wager. The journey's expenses leave him with little monetary gain, and he shares what remains with Passepartout and even Fix. Fogg marries Aouda, recognizing that the voyage has given him a happiness that his former regulated life lacked.

characters.description: The SecUnit from the survey contract, now traveling alone and disguising itself as an augmented human. It is working its way toward RaviHyral, the mining installation where, according to the record, it killed the humans it was assigned to protect before its memory of the event was erased. It wants to know whether that is what happened. It has no owner supervising it, no legitimate identity, and a constant need to avoid the scans that would expose it as a construct.
characters.name: Murderbot

characters.description: The bot pilot of a large university research transport, vastly more capable than the cargo bots the SecUnit has been riding with, and travelling between assignments with its crew off ship. It notices its stowaway immediately and bargains rather than reporting it: company, conversation and shared entertainment serials in exchange for help. It is arrogant, invasive, alarmingly powerful and better at planning than the SecUnit is. The SecUnit gives it a rude nickname and shortens it to ART.
characters.name: ART

characters.description: One of three junior technicians stranded on the transit station after the woman they worked for on the installation below kept the results of their project and paid them nothing. Young, stubborn and out of money, she hires the SecUnit, whom she takes for a human security consultant, to protect the group while they try to get their work back.
characters.name: Tapan

characters.description: One of Tapan's two colleagues, part of the same group of junior technicians cheated out of their project and their pay.
characters.name: Rami

characters.description: The third member of the group of junior technicians, and the most reluctant to go anywhere near their former employer again.
characters.name: Maro

characters.description: The businesswoman on the installation who employed the three technicians, kept the product of their work, and has no intention of handing it back. She has money, hired security of her own, and the habit of treating junior staff and constructs alike as disposable.
characters.name: Tlacey

characters.description: A construct owned by Tlacey and built for sexual companionship, kept obedient by exactly the kind of governor module the SecUnit freed itself from, and used by its owner as a courier and an informant. Its situation puts a question to the SecUnit that it would rather not answer: what it owes another construct that is still controlled.
characters.name: The ComfortUnit

characters.description: One of two heavily augmented human security operatives working for Tlacey, hired for the work ordinary guards will not do. Equipped for combat and contemptuous of the security consultant they take the SecUnit to be, Wilken works alongside a long-standing partner, Gerth.
characters.name: Wilken

recaps.ending: Tlacey is dead, killed by the ComfortUnit she owned once the SecUnit removes the governor module holding it; the freed construct takes what it needs from her operation and goes its own way. The surviving technicians, Tapan and Maro, recover their work and leave the installation with enough to start again. The SecUnit has its answer about RaviHyral: it did cause the deaths, but through a catastrophic system failure rather than a decision, and the corporation that owned it deleted the record and resold it rather than account for the conditions that produced it. The knowledge does not absolve it, and it concludes that it does not need to be absolved. Back aboard the research transport, ART repairs it and offers to keep it on permanently, since ART's own crew are not due back for a while and it would rather not be alone. The SecUnit refuses. It has read in the newsfeeds that Dr. Mensah and Preservation are locked in a legal fight with GrayCris, the company that tried to kill her team, and that GrayCris is dangerous to her. It takes a fresh fabricated identity and leaves to gather proof of what GrayCris was really doing, with the friendship left open rather than finished.
recaps.in_short: Traveling alone after leaving the survey team, the SecUnit heads for RaviHyral, the mining installation where the record says it killed the humans it was guarding before its memory was erased. It hitches a ride on a university research transport whose bot pilot, which it nicknames ART, is far more capable than it expected; ART trades help for company, alters its body so scans read it as an augmented human, and joins the investigation. To get down to the mine, the SecUnit takes a job protecting three young technicians whose former employer, Tlacey, stole their work. The exchange she offers is a trap, one of the three is killed, and the SecUnit stops pretending to be human: it dismantles Tlacey's security, frees the ComfortUnit she keeps under a governor module, and that construct kills her. Underground, the SecUnit recovers the lost memory and learns that it did cause the deaths, but through a system failure rather than a choice, and that its owners erased the evidence and resold it. It parts from ART and sets off to find evidence against GrayCris for Dr. Mensah.

recaps.text: Previously: the narrator is a SecUnit, a security construct that secretly disabled its own governor module and can no longer be controlled by the corporation that owns it. On a planetary survey contract it kept a small research team alive against a rival company, GrayCris, which was killing witnesses to an illegal alien remnant salvage operation, and in the process the team learned what it was. Dr. Mensah, who led them, bought the unit to stop the company destroying it and offered to take it home to Preservation, where it would be free. It left instead, alone, on a cargo transport. It carries one unanswered question: the record says that at a mining installation called RaviHyral it went wrong and killed the humans it was assigned to guard, and its memory of that day was deleted afterwards. It is traveling toward the installation to find out whether it is a murderer.

Riding automated cargo transports as an unnoticed passenger, the SecUnit works its way toward RaviHyral. It boards a large university research transport whose bot pilot is far more intelligent than anything it has dealt with, spots it at once, and, being alone and bored while its crew is away, offers a deal instead of an alarm: company, conversation and shared entertainment serials in return for help. The SecUnit nicknames it ART. ART examines the deleted region of its memory, agrees to help it reach the installation, and uses the transport's medical systems to alter the unit's body so that scans will read it as an augmented human rather than as a construct. Arriving at the transit station above RaviHyral with a fabricated identity and nothing visibly dangerous about it, the SecUnit still needs a plausible reason to travel down to the mine, and starts looking for one.

The cover it finds is a job. Three young technicians, Tapan, Rami and Maro, are stranded on the station after the woman they worked for on the installation, Tlacey, kept the results of their project and paid them nothing. They hire the SecUnit as a security consultant, believing it to be human, to protect them while they try to recover their work. It travels down with them, keeping ART on the comm and its own capabilities hidden. Tlacey agrees to an exchange, but her preparations make plain that she has no intention of returning anything, and considerable interest in the unusually effective consultant her former employees have acquired. She also has professional muscle of her own, and a ComfortUnit, another construct held under a governor module, which she uses to carry messages and watch people. The SecUnit works out that the meeting being arranged is a trap and cannot talk its clients out of it.

The exchange goes as badly as expected: Tlacey's people kill Rami. The SecUnit gets Tapan and Maro clear and drops its pretence of being human, and with ART's help it goes after Tlacey's operation directly. Her two augmented security operatives are outmatched once the SecUnit stops pretending, and the ComfortUnit, whose governor module the SecUnit removes, kills Tlacey itself and leaves free. In the mine's abandoned levels the SecUnit finally recovers what happened at RaviHyral: the deaths were real and it was what killed the miners, but the cause was a catastrophic failure of the installation's systems and of its own control module rather than any decision it made, and the company that owned it wiped the record and resold it instead of answering for it. Tapan and Maro get their work back and passage out. The SecUnit returns to ART, which asks it to stay; it refuses, having learned that Dr. Mensah is in a legal fight with GrayCris, and sets off alone to find evidence she can use.

characters.description: FitzChivalry Farseer, lately acknowledged as a prince of the Six Duchies and no longer interested in being one. He believes his younger daughter was murdered, he has a hand full of Silver that unmakes whatever it touches unprotected, and he is travelling south with one purpose: to destroy the Servants of Clerres entirely. He is past fifty, damaged by years of Skill use, and better at killing than at anything else he has ever been asked to do.
characters.name: FitzChivalry Farseer

characters.description: Fitz and Molly's younger daughter, about ten years old and small for far less than that, stranded thousands of miles from home in an Elderling city after months lost inside the Skill-pillars. She dreams true, writes everything down, and has survived captivity by being underestimated. Her captors believe she is the awaited one of their prophecies.
characters.name: Bee

characters.description: The White Prophet, healed in body but still blind, travelling south in disguise with Fitz. He grew up inside Clerres, knows its walls, its people and its habits, and wants every one of them dead. He is also keeping things from Fitz, as he always has.
characters.name: The Fool

characters.description: Chade's acknowledged son, a scribe and swordsman of moderate talent who failed to protect Withywoods and has come along to make up for it. He is loyal, unlucky and out of his element on every leg of the journey.
characters.name: FitzVigilant

characters.description: Chade's apprentice, trained in poisons, disguise and quiet violence, who has spent years being taken for a boy and finds it useful. Young, quick and entirely at home in a conspiracy.
characters.name: Spark

characters.description: The Withywoods stable boy who survived the raid, attached himself to Fitz's household and refuses to be sent home. He is the only member of the party who never stopped believing Bee might be alive.
characters.name: Perseverance

characters.description: The Servant who led the raid on Withywoods, stranded far from Clerres with her prize and her prophecy and very little else. Her certainty has survived being lost in the Skill-pillars, and she still intends to deliver Bee to the order that raised her.
characters.name: Dwalia

characters.description: The pale Servant whose fog can make people forget what they are looking at and believe what he wants them to believe. He is powerful, childlike and desperate to be wanted, and Bee has learned exactly where those two things meet.
characters.name: Vindeliar

characters.description: An Elderling and the effective ruler of Kelsingra, once a Bingtown Trader's daughter. She takes in a starving foreign child and a party of strangers who came out of a Skill-pillar and begins working out which of them are prisoners and which are jailers.
characters.name: Malta Khuprus

characters.description: A liveship with a hacked-off face and a violent history, built of wizardwood that was never wood at all. He has capsized, killed crews, been abandoned on a beach and been salvaged, and he is not one person: there is more than one mind in his timbers, and all of them remember being something other than a ship.
characters.name: Paragon

characters.description: A Bingtown Trader's daughter who spent her youth fighting for the right to sail her family's liveship and has been at sea ever since. Blunt, seasoned and unimpressed by rank, she knows the Fool by an older acquaintance and an older name.
characters.name: Althea Vestrit

characters.description: Captain of the liveship Paragon, a disowned Trader's son who made himself a sailor the hard way. He is Althea's husband and the only man who has ever kept Paragon sailing for long.
characters.name: Brashen Trell

characters.description: The son of the pirate king Kennit and the Pirate Isles' reigning queen, handsome, headstrong and deeply unwilling to inherit a throne he never asked for or a father's reputation he does not admire.
characters.name: Kennitsson

characters.description: Ruler of the Pirate Isles, once a whore aboard a pirate ship and now a queen who governs by force of will. She built a kingdom out of her dead husband's legend and intends her son to keep it.
characters.name: Etta

characters.description: The ruling council of Clerres: a handful of Servants who own a walled island fortress, a school, a breeding programme for prophets, and a trade in selling futures to anyone who can pay. They are old, comfortable, and accustomed to being obeyed by everyone within their walls.
characters.name: The Four

characters.description: A dark-skinned man who was a White Prophet in an age long past, and who went south with the Fool when both of them left the Six Duchies. He has been at Clerres a long time and not by choice.
characters.name: Prilkop

recaps.ending: Clerres is destroyed. Fitz poisons, burns and cuts his way through the fortress, the Four are killed, the school and its records go up, and Dwalia and Vindeliar both die there. Bee is found alive, and father and daughter are reunited in the ruins of the place that took her. Prilkop is freed. Paragon keeps his side of the bargain, carries the survivors clear, and is then allowed to become what his timbers always were, separating into dragons and leaving the sea. The party comes home the long way, by liveship to Bingtown and up the Rain Wild River, and Bee is acknowledged as a Farseer, a princess of the Six Duchies in her own right. Fitz does not recover. The Silver, the Skill and the wounds he took at Clerres have used him up, and he is dying by inches; the Fool, who has spent his life spending Fitz, cannot mend him this time. Fitz goes to the Mountain Kingdom, to the quarry where Verity carved his dragon, and gives himself to the stone as the Skilled have always been able to do, pouring his memories and his self into it and finding his wolf waiting there. Bee goes home to Withywoods with the Fool, who stays to raise her, and with Nettle, Riddle, Lant, Spark and Perseverance around her. The Servants are finished, the prophecies they farmed are over, and Bee is left with her father's journals, her own dreams, and a wolf in the woods.
recaps.in_short: Believing Bee dead, Fitz sails south with the Fool, Lant, Spark and Perseverance to destroy the Servants of Clerres, taking passage on the mad liveship Paragon with Althea and Brashen Trell. Bee, meanwhile, is alive: recovered at Kelsingra among the Elderlings, then dragged away again by Dwalia and shipped across the world to Clerres, where the Servants examine her as the fulfilment of their prophecies. Fitz's party crosses the Pirate Isles and the southern sea, Paragon bargaining for a future of his own in exchange for the voyage, and reaches the island fortress. Fitz and the Fool go in and take it apart: poison, fire and murder, the ruling Four killed, the school destroyed, Dwalia and Vindeliar dead. In the ruins Fitz finds Bee alive. Paragon carries them clear and is released to become dragons; the survivors sail home by way of Bingtown and the Rain Wild River, and Bee is acknowledged as a Farseer princess. But Fitz is dying of what the Silver and the Skill and Clerres cost him. He goes to the Mountain quarry where Verity carved his dragon, gives his memories and himself into the stone, and finds his wolf there. Bee goes home to Withywoods with the Fool to raise her.

recaps.text: Previously: FitzChivalry Farseer, royal bastard, assassin and Skill user, was left for dead by the usurper Regal, survived by hiding his mind in his wolf Nighteyes, and let the world bury him; Molly married the stablemaster Burrich and raised Fitz's daughter Nettle as Burrich's own. Guided by the Fool, the White Prophet who named him Catalyst, he helped end the Red Ship war. In the Tawny Man trilogy he returned secretly to court, and on the ice island of Aslevjal the Fool was tortured to death by the Pale Woman and brought back by Fitz through the Skill; the dragon Icefyre was freed and dragons returned to the world. The Fool then left the Six Duchies for the south with Prilkop, an older White Prophet. Fitz married Molly at last and lived twenty quiet years at Withywoods. In Fool's Assassin Molly bore a late, tiny daughter, Bee, who seemed simple and was in fact brilliant and prophetic, and then died; and the Fool returned to Buckkeep blinded and broken by the Servants of Clerres, the order that bred him, warning of an unexpected son they hunted. While Fitz tended him, Servants and Chalcedean mercenaries raided Withywoods behind a fog that erased memory and carried Bee off. In Fool's Quest Fitz healed the Fool with Silver from Chade's secret store, silvering his own hand, then hunted the raiders across the kingdom and destroyed their camp, rescuing Shine but arriving moments after Dwalia took Bee into a Skill-pillar. Convinced his daughter was dead, he was publicly acknowledged as Prince FitzChivalry Farseer and set out south with the Fool, Lant, Spark and Perseverance to annihilate Clerres. Bee, lost inside the pillars for months, emerged alive at Kelsingra, the Elderling city on the Rain Wild River, still a prisoner of Dwalia and still the Shaysim of the Servants' prophecies, with no one who loved her knowing she lived.

Bee is nursed back from starvation at Kelsingra among Elderlings and dragons, a world she knows only from books. Malta Khuprus works out quickly that the child who fell out of a Skill-pillar is not a member of the party that came with her, and that the pale strangers are her jailers, but Vindeliar's fog makes the truth slippery for everyone around him. Far to the north, Fitz's party travels south with a Silver-gloved hand and a plan that is not really a plan: get to Clerres, kill everyone, and do not expect to return. Fitz's Silver touch is a weapon he cannot control, capable of unmaking whatever it touches, and it is also slowly killing him.

Bee is taken out of Kelsingra again. Dwalia gets her away downriver, and the child who was almost safe is back in the hands of the order that stole her, being carried through the Rain Wilds toward the sea and the long voyage to Clerres. She keeps writing, keeps watching, and keeps working on Vindeliar, the only crack in her captors' arrangements. Fitz's party comes down through the Mountains and out to the coast, where the world grows unfamiliar: dragons in the sky, liveships in the harbours, and southern politics that owe the Six Duchies nothing. The distance between father and daughter narrows and neither of them knows it.

At Bingtown the party takes passage on the liveship Paragon, captained by Brashen Trell and sailed by Althea Vestrit, with the pirate heir Kennitsson aboard. The Fool travels openly as Amber, a woman these people knew years ago and remember with mixed feelings, and Fitz becomes her servant again, which suits neither of them. Paragon is not a stable vessel: he is mad, violent, and made from wizardwood that holds more than one mind, none of which was ever human. He agrees to carry them across the southern sea, but on his own terms, and the bargain he strikes is about what he is to be allowed to become when the voyage is over.

The voyage runs through the Pirate Isles, where Etta rules the kingdom her dead husband built and where her son's future is decided over his objections, and out into open water among sea serpents and the ships that hunt them. Aboard Paragon the party rubs against a crew that did not sign on for an assassination, and Amber's secrets and Fitz's temper both cost them. Bee, on another ship on another route, is shipped south as cargo, sustained by her own stubbornness and by the hold she has quietly taken on Vindeliar. Both journeys converge on the same island.

Bee reaches Clerres and is delivered to the Servants, who have waited a long time for the child their prophecies promised. What they do with her is examination rather than ceremony: she is caged, questioned, catalogued and mined for dreams, and she learns what the order actually is, a walled school that breeds prophets, farms their visions, and sells futures to anyone rich enough to buy one. Fitz and Amber arrive at the island and begin scouting a fortress Amber grew up inside, buying information, bribing where they can, and finding that the place is far better defended and far more populous than a vengeance party of five can handle.

The reconnaissance goes wrong. Clerres notices strangers asking questions, the harbour stops being safe, and the party's cover comes apart in accusations and closed gates. Amber's plans and Fitz's plans turn out not to be the same plans, and the cost of that lands on the people who came along out of loyalty. Inside the walls, Bee is one prisoner among many, and the Servants' internal rivalries prove as dangerous to her as their intentions. Prilkop, the White Prophet who went south with the Fool decades ago, is found to be held there too. The party has to get inside a fortress that is now expecting them.

They get in, and Fitz does what he was trained for on a scale nobody asked for. Poison goes into the food and drink of an entire fortress, fires are set, and the assassin the Six Duchies made forty years ago works through Clerres room by room. The Four are confronted and killed, the school's records and its stores of dreams burn, and the order that has been selling the future for generations is destroyed in a night. It is not a clean operation and Fitz does not try to make it one; a great many people die who were never anything but the Servants' property.

In the wreckage Fitz finds Bee alive, and the death he has been avenging for a year turns out never to have happened. Dwalia and Vindeliar both die at Clerres. Prilkop is freed. The survivors fight their way back to the harbour, and Paragon keeps his side of the bargain: he carries them clear, and is then released to become what his timbers always were, separating into dragons and leaving the sea for the sky. Fitz, however, is failing. Between the Silver, the Skill and what Clerres cost him physically, he is being consumed, and neither the Fool nor his own coterie can stop it.

The long way home runs by liveship to Bingtown and up the Rain Wild River, past Kelsingra and its dragons, and back toward the Six Duchies. Bee, who spent a year as a prisoner and a prophecy, is acknowledged as a Farseer and a princess of the realm in her own right, with Nettle, Riddle, Lant, Spark and Perseverance around her. Fitz spends the journey dying, held together by the Skill and by people who will not let go of him, and knowing perfectly well what is happening. He puts his affairs in order and tells his daughter what he can while he can still do it.

Fitz goes to the Mountain Kingdom, to the quarry where Verity carved his dragon out of memory-stone, and does what the Skilled have always been able to do at the end: he gives himself to the stone, pouring his memories, his self and his long life into it rather than simply stopping. Nighteyes is waiting there, and what he becomes is neither a man nor a ghost but something with a wolf's heart in it. Bee goes home to Withywoods with the Fool, who stays to raise her, and inherits her father's journals, her mother's house and her own true dreams. The Servants are finished and their prophecies with them; the White Prophet's work is over; and in the woods around Bee's home there is a wolf.

characters.description: The Farseer bastard, officially dead and buried. He survived Regal's dungeons by retreating into his wolf as his body died, and he has been coaxed back into it over a winter by Burrich and Chade. He is half-wild, easier as a wolf than as a man, with a body ruined by torture and poison and a memory full of gaps. Nothing binds him to the crown any more: the king he swore to is dead, the prince he served is believed dead, and the woman he loved is gone. What he has instead is a single fixed intention, to find Regal and kill him.
characters.name: FitzChivalry Farseer

characters.description: The wolf Fitz bought caged in Buckkeep Town and bonded with through the Wit. He is now full-grown and the bond is total: they share senses, thoughts and, for a time, a body. He is blunt, sardonic and impatient with human tangles, wanting only a pack, a hunt and a place to sleep, and he stays because Fitz is his pack, not because he approves of anything Fitz intends to do.
characters.name: Nighteyes

characters.description: Buckkeep's former stablemaster, who dug Fitz out of his grave and spent the winter dragging him back into a man's shape. Driven out of Buckkeep by Regal's men, lamed, jobless and drinking, he has kept Fitz alive at enormous cost and expects to be obeyed for it. He believes Fitz should go to Kettricken and the Mountains rather than after Regal, and the disagreement is bitter.
characters.name: Burrich

characters.description: The old assassin who trained Fitz, now out of the walls of Buckkeep and living rough, running what is left of a loyalist network for a queen who is over the mountains and a king everyone believes dead. He is exhausted and grimly practical, and he too thinks Fitz should serve the Farseers rather than his own grudge.
characters.name: Chade Fallstar

characters.description: The chandler's daughter Fitz grew up loving, who left Buckkeep without telling him where she was going. She believes him dead, along with everyone else. She exists in this book first as the life Fitz did not get to have.
characters.name: Molly

characters.description: Chivalry's widow, who buried Fitz and grieves him, and who holds Buckkeep Town and its defences together with almost no money and no authority while the crown sits inland at Tradeford. Scattered and stubborn as ever, she turns out to be formidable when there is nobody else left to do the work.
characters.name: Lady Patience

characters.description: The youngest Farseer, now crowned king. He has moved the court inland to Tradeford, stripped Buckkeep of everything portable and left the coastal duchies to defend themselves against the Red Ships. He rules through a Skill coterie of his own, has made the Wit a capital crime and hunts those who carry it, and he had Fitz tortured and condemned.
characters.name: King Regal

characters.description: A travelling minstrel, young, ambitious and short of patrons, working the roads between the coast and the inland duchies. She is quick, unsentimental and entirely clear about what she wants: to witness an event worth a song and so make her name. She recognizes more about her fellow traveller than is comfortable and treats the knowledge as an opportunity.
characters.name: Starling Birdsong

characters.description: An old woman travelling with a party of pilgrims bound for the Mountain Kingdom, small, dry and blunt, who passes the miles at a stone game few people can play well. She is sharper than her years suggest, asks questions that are far too well aimed, and clearly understands things about magic that an ordinary devout old woman would have no way of knowing.
characters.name: Kettle

characters.description: Queen of the Six Duchies in exile, back in her father's country and mourning both her husband and the child she lost. She holds herself to the Mountain idea of the ruler as Sacrifice and is preparing to go herself in search of Verity, on almost no evidence and with almost no help, because nobody else will.
characters.name: Kettricken

characters.description: The former court jester, who fled Buckkeep with Kettricken and lives in the Mountain Kingdom carving wood and keeping the queen company. Away from Buckkeep the mockery is thinner and the seriousness underneath it plainer: the Fool speaks of being a White Prophet, sent to turn the world onto a better course, and of Fitz as the Catalyst whose choices do the turning. Fiercely attached to Fitz and grieved at having believed him dead.
characters.name: The Fool

characters.description: The most able of the Skill coterie Galen trained, now the chief instrument of Regal's rule. Patient and quiet, he hunts Fitz through the Skill itself, reaching for him whenever Fitz's guard slips, and he is far stronger in the magic than Fitz has ever been.
characters.name: Will

characters.description: The rightful King of the Six Duchies, missing for over a year beyond the Mountain Kingdom. He reaches Fitz through the Skill in brief, overwhelming contacts carrying a single command, to come to him. What is left of the plain, dutiful soldier who rode out of Buckkeep is a question the journey is undertaken to answer.
characters.name: Verity Farseer

characters.description: A small daughter born to Molly, being raised in a cottage far from Buckkeep. Fitz learns of her existence through the Skill, long after the fact and from a distance, and can do nothing about it.
characters.name: Nettle

recaps.ending: Verity finishes his dragon by pouring the last of himself into it, and the black stone rises as a living creature carrying him. Kettle gives herself to the unfinished dragon she has spent her life owing a debt to, and other members of the party pay their own prices. Fitz kills Will, taking the coterie's Skill knowledge as he does it, and then reaches into Regal's mind and rewrites him, binding him to serve Queen Kettricken and stripping out his hatred of Fitz entirely, which ends the civil war without another battle. Fitz then wakes the old stone dragons sleeping in the Six Duchies by feeding them memories of his own, and the dragons drive the Red Ships from the coast and end the raiding war. Kettricken returns to Buckkeep as reigning queen, carrying Verity's heir, with Chade and Patience to help her rebuild a stripped and half-ruined kingdom. Verity does not come back as a man. Fitz, still officially dead, makes the choice the whole book has been pushing him towards and stays dead: Molly has a life with Burrich and a daughter who calls Burrich father, and Fitz will not walk into it and break it. He parts from the Fool, keeps Nighteyes, and disappears to a quiet place to write the histories of the war nobody knows he fought. The Farseer line is secure, the coast is free, and the man who bought all of it has given up every claim on his own name.
recaps.in_short: Fitz comes back from the grave half a wolf and spends a winter being coaxed into a man again by Burrich and Chade, then leaves them both to go inland and kill Regal. The attempt fails, and in the middle of it Verity reaches him through the Skill with a single overriding command, to come to him. Compelled, Fitz travels to the Mountain Kingdom with the minstrel Starling and an old pilgrim woman, Kettle, who knows far more about the Skill than she admits, and finds Kettricken and the Fool. The party takes the ancient Skill road beyond the mountains and finds Verity in a stone quarry, carving a dragon and pouring his life into it: the Elderlings of legend are stone dragons, quickened by the people who make them. Through the Skill Fitz sees that Molly is living with Burrich and has borne his daughter, and gives them up. Verity fathers an heir on Kettricken using Fitz's body, then completes his dragon and flies. Fitz kills Will, Skill-commands Regal into loyalty, and wakes the sleeping dragons of the Six Duchies, who end the Red Ship war. Kettricken rules; Fitz stays dead and disappears with his wolf.

recaps.text: Previously in the Farseer trilogy: FitzChivalry, bastard son of the abdicated Prince Chivalry, was raised in the Buckkeep stables by the stableman Burrich and secretly trained as King Shrewd's assassin by Chade. He carried two magics, the forbidden animal-bond of the Wit and the royal Skill, which the Skillmaster Galen deliberately crippled in him. Outislander Red Ships raided the coast and returned their hostages Forged, emptied of all human feeling. Prince Verity, the King-in-Waiting, burned himself out using the Skill against the raiders and finally rode away beyond the Mountain Kingdom to seek the Elderlings, legendary allies from an older war, leaving his Mountain-born queen Kettricken behind. His younger brother Regal used the absence: he had himself named heir, drained and then murdered the failing King Shrewd through his tame Skill coterie, and stripped Buckkeep to move the court inland, abandoning the coast. Fitz killed two of the coterie in front of the court, was tortured and condemned, and escaped death only by retreating into his bonded wolf Nighteyes while his body died; Burrich and Chade dug him up and brought him back. Kettricken, who had lost Verity's child, fled to the Mountains with the Fool. Molly, Fitz's lover, had already left him without a word. Regal was crowned, the Wit became a hanging matter, and Fitz, officially a corpse, was free of every oath he had ever taken.

Fitz spends the winter in a hut with Burrich, more wolf than man, having to be taught again how to speak, cook and behave as a person. The crossing into Nighteyes has left him with gaps in his memory and a preference for the simpler shape; Burrich, lamed and driven out of Buckkeep, drinks and bullies him back into humanity anyway. Chade comes with news: Regal is crowned and sitting inland at Tradeford, the coastal duchies have been left to face the Red Ships alone, Buckkeep is stripped and Patience is holding its town together on nothing, and Kettricken is in the Mountain Kingdom. Both men want Fitz to go to the queen and serve the Farseer line. Fitz wants Regal dead. The argument ends the household: he takes almost nothing, leaves Burrich behind, and starts inland with only Nighteyes for company.

Fitz works his way inland by hiring out as a labourer and a horse-hand, keeping his name and his wolf hidden. The further from the coast he goes, the stranger the country becomes to him: the inland duchies have never seen a Red Ship, are prospering under Regal, and believe the coast's suffering is exaggerated. He learns that Regal has made the Wit a capital crime and that people suspected of it are being hunted and killed. He falls in with the minstrel Starling Birdsong, who is travelling the same roads looking for an event worth a song, works out far too much about him, and attaches herself to him rather than turning him in. Fitz's Skill remains unreliable, opening at the wrong moments and letting Regal's coterie feel for him, and he dulls it with a herb that costs him more each time.

Fitz reaches Tradeford, the inland seat where Regal has installed his court with everything he took from Buckkeep. He gets himself hired into the grounds and spends days learning the household, the guard rota and the king's habits, and confirming that the coterie is the real power around Regal. He also sees at close hand how comfortable the inland duchies are while the coast burns. Working alone, half-broken and dependent on a wolf who does not understand vengeance, he sets up his attempt on the king, knowing he is unlikely to survive it and no longer greatly caring.

The attempt on Regal fails. Fitz kills men trying to reach him, is badly hurt, and is saved only because Verity chooses that moment to reach him through the Skill with an overwhelming command: come to me. The compulsion is not an invitation but an order, and Fitz can neither disobey it nor stop feeling it. He escapes Tradeford barely alive and turns towards the Mountain Kingdom, driven by a summons from a man everyone believes dead. Travelling as a servant with a party of pilgrims bound for the mountains, he falls in with an old woman named Kettle, who plays a difficult stone game, asks questions that are far too well aimed, and plainly knows things about the Skill that no devout old traveller should know.

The road to the Mountain Kingdom is dangerous in its own right: Regal has soldiers on it, the border is effectively at war because he blames the Mountains for Verity's disappearance, and Will hunts Fitz through the Skill whenever his guard drops. Fitz, Starling, Kettle and Nighteyes get through, and at Jhaampe Fitz finds Kettricken and the Fool, both of whom have mourned him. Kettricken is preparing to go in search of Verity herself, with a map, a handful of people and the Mountain conviction that a ruler is spent for the good of the people. The Fool, out of Buckkeep and out of motley, speaks plainly for the first time about what he believes himself to be, a White Prophet sent to shift the world onto a better course, and about Fitz as the Catalyst through whom the shifting happens.

The party sets out beyond the mountains along an ancient road built by a vanished people, following the map Verity used. The road itself is made of a stuff that drags at the mind and pulls a Skill user out of himself, and travellers on it lose their way in their own heads. Kettle, who has been quietly protecting Fitz from the coterie's attacks, admits what she is: she belonged to a coterie of her own an age ago, has lived far longer than a woman should, and carries a debt she came here to pay. She teaches Fitz to guard his mind with the stone game. The road brings them to a quarry of black stone littered with half-finished dragons, and there they find Verity: alive, filthy, hollowed out, and carving.

The Elderlings of Six Duchies legend are dragons of black stone, and they are made: a carver fills the stone with his own memories and life until it wakes and flies. Verity has been at his for a year, has poured most of himself into it and has little left over for his wife or his kingdom. Kettricken, who crossed the mountains for him, is met by a man who can barely remember how to want her. While the party works and guards the quarry, Fitz forces his damaged Skill open and reaches for the people he left behind, and finds Molly in a cottage with a baby daughter and with Burrich, who has taken the place Fitz vacated by dying. He cannot argue, cannot appear and cannot even be angry with justice, and it very nearly finishes him.

The Farseer line needs an heir and Verity has nothing human left to give. With Kettricken's consent, he takes Fitz's body for a night through the Skill and lies with his wife in it, and Kettricken conceives. Fitz is left to live with having been used as an instrument one more time, this time to the marrow. Regal's coterie closes on the quarry, and Will comes in person as well as through the Skill; the party's defences are the stone game, Kettle's old knowledge and Verity's failing attention. Kettle finishes settling her ancient debt with a dragon of her own. Verity carves on towards an end that will not leave a man behind, and the quarry becomes the last battlefield of the civil war.

Verity spends the last of himself, and his dragon rises and flies with him in it. In the fighting at the quarry Fitz kills Will and strips the coterie's Skill knowledge out of him as he dies; the rest of Regal's coterie is broken. Fitz then reaches Regal's mind directly and rewrites it, binding him to serve Queen Kettricken faithfully and removing his hatred of Fitz altogether, which ends the civil war without another battle. Fitz goes on to wake the old stone dragons sleeping across the Six Duchies, feeding them memories of his own life to quicken them, and the dragons sweep the Red Ships from the coast and end the raiding war. Kettricken returns to Buckkeep as reigning queen with Verity's heir on the way, to rebuild a stripped kingdom with Chade and Patience beside her. Fitz makes the last choice himself: Molly has a daughter and a life with Burrich, and he will not walk back into it. He parts from the Fool, keeps Nighteyes, and vanishes to live quietly and write down the history of a war he fought as a dead man.

characters.description: The thirteen-year-old youngest child of the Tallis family, an aspiring writer with a powerful appetite for order and drama. She prepares a play for her brother's homecoming and interprets the adults around her through the stories she already knows, often treating uncertain events as if they must have a single clear meaning.
characters.name: Briony Tallis

characters.description: Briony's older sister, recently returned from Cambridge and uncertain what to do next. Intelligent and restless, she is frustrated by the atmosphere of the family home and by her unsettled relationship with Robbie, the childhood companion who grew up beside her.
characters.name: Cecilia Tallis

characters.description: The son of the Tallis family's cleaning woman and a childhood friend of Cecilia. The Tallises have supported his education, and he has excelled at Cambridge. He hopes to study medicine, but his easy place near the family is complicated by class and by his unsettled relationship with Cecilia.
characters.name: Robbie Turner

characters.description: Briony's fifteen-year-old cousin, sent to the Tallis home with her younger twin brothers while her parents separate. Precocious and self-possessed in Briony's eyes, she takes the leading role in the play and resents the disruption caused by her brothers.
characters.name: Lola Quincey

characters.description: Lola's nine-year-old twin brothers, visiting the Tallis household during their parents' marital crisis. Frightened and homesick beneath their unruly behavior, they are assigned parts in Briony's play but have little patience for her strict direction.
characters.name: Jackson and Pierrot Quincey

characters.description: The frequently bedridden mother of Briony, Cecilia, and Leon. Migraines keep her withdrawn from much of the household activity, but she listens closely to the sounds of the house and takes pride in Briony's apparent seriousness and good sense.
characters.name: Emily Tallis

characters.description: The eldest Tallis child, returning from London for a summer visit. Sociable and less burdened by the tensions of the household than his sisters, he brings his wealthy friend Paul Marshall with him.
characters.name: Leon Tallis

characters.description: A wealthy friend of Leon who manufactures chocolate and hopes for a lucrative army contract. Confident and attentive to his hosts, he arrives at the Tallis estate as Leon's guest for the family dinner.
characters.name: Paul Marshall

characters.description: Robbie's mother, who works for the Tallis family and lives in a cottage on their property. Proud of her son's achievements, she is conscious that the family's generosity has never erased the social distance between them.
characters.name: Grace Turner

characters.description: A fellow private in the British army who retreats across France with Robbie in 1940. Practical, talkative, and experienced, he helps keep their small group moving toward Dunkirk as the military withdrawal breaks down around them.
characters.name: Nettle

characters.description: The third soldier in Robbie and Nettle's group during the retreat to Dunkirk. Older and quieter than Nettle, he shares the work of navigation and survival as they cross a landscape crowded with refugees and retreating troops.
characters.name: Mace

characters.description: A strict senior nurse responsible for training Briony and the other probationers at a London hospital during the war. She demands exact obedience and suppresses personal distinctions in order to prepare them for exhausting clinical work.
characters.name: Sister Drummond

recaps.ending: In 1999, Briony is a celebrated novelist facing the onset of vascular dementia. She has completed the final version of the book that recounts the events begun at the Tallis estate. She reveals that the scene in which she visited Cecilia and Robbie and promised to retract her accusation did not happen. Robbie died of septicemia at Bray Dunes before the Dunkirk evacuation, and Cecilia died later that year in the bombing of Balham Underground station. Lola and Paul Marshall remained married and became influential public figures; because they are still alive, Briony cannot publish an account naming them without legal danger. Her novel gives Robbie and Cecilia the shared future reality denied them. She regards that imagined reunion as the only reparation her art can now make, while recognizing that an author who controls the story cannot grant herself an objective pardon.
recaps.in_short: At a country estate in 1935, thirteen-year-old Briony Tallis misreads the developing love between her sister Cecilia and Robbie Turner, the housekeeper's educated son. After Briony's cousin Lola is assaulted in the dark, Briony confidently identifies Robbie, although she did not see the attacker's face. Robbie is imprisoned while the actual assailant, Paul Marshall, later marries Lola. During the war Robbie joins the army and retreats toward Dunkirk; Cecilia becomes a nurse and rejects her family, and Briony also trains as a nurse while trying to confront what she did. A later account of Briony visiting the reunited lovers and promising to recant is revealed as fiction. Robbie died in France and Cecilia died months later in a London bombing. The elderly Briony has written their story as an act of atonement, giving them in art the life together they never had.

recaps.text: In the summer of 1935, thirteen-year-old Briony Tallis prepares a play to celebrate the return of her older brother Leon to the family's country estate. She recruits her visiting cousins Lola and the twins Jackson and Pierrot, but rehearsal exposes their homesickness and her need to control every detail. Briony's older sister Cecilia is also home from Cambridge, restless and uncertain about her future. Robbie Turner, the highly educated son of the family's cleaning woman, lives nearby and hopes to study medicine. Cecilia and Robbie have known each other since childhood, but their relationship has become tense. Leon arrives with Paul Marshall, a wealthy chocolate manufacturer. The household gathers for dinner while Briony watches the adults with the confidence that their behavior can be arranged into the kinds of moral patterns she finds in stories.

A quarrel between Cecilia and Robbie beside a fountain ends with part of a valuable vase broken in the water. Cecilia strips to her underwear to retrieve the pieces and dives in, while Robbie watches helplessly. Briony sees the scene from a window and interprets it as a strange act of power by Robbie rather than the awkward result of an argument. Robbie later writes Cecilia a formal apology, but he also types a sexually explicit version that he never intends to send. He asks Briony to deliver the letter and accidentally gives her the explicit draft. Briony reads it. Already disturbed by what she saw at the fountain, she decides the message reveals something dangerous about Robbie. Cecilia reads the note and, after her initial shock, recognizes that it expresses the desire between them.

Before dinner, Briony enters the library and sees Cecilia and Robbie having sex. Because she lacks the context of their mutual attraction and has already judged Robbie through his letter, she believes she is witnessing an assault. During the oppressive family dinner, the twins run away, leaving a note that prompts the household to spread across the dark grounds in search of them. Briony encounters Lola after someone has attacked her beside the lake. The assailant flees before Briony can see him clearly. Lola is confused and injured, and does not make a firm identification. Briony nevertheless connects the assault to her existing theory about Robbie and begins to turn her interpretation into certainty.

Police question the household about Lola's assault. Briony repeatedly names Robbie and comes to present inference as direct recognition, while Lola gradually stops resisting that account. Cecilia insists Robbie is innocent, but the explicit letter and Briony's description of the library scene make the accusation persuasive to the adults. Robbie returns carrying one of the missing twins, having found the boys safely, yet he is arrested rather than thanked. Grace Turner condemns the Tallises for accepting the charge, and Cecilia openly sides with Robbie against her family. The evidence against him rests on Briony's confidence rather than a clear sighting. Paul Marshall, who was also present at the estate and had earlier approached Lola, escapes serious suspicion.

Five years later, Robbie is serving as a private in the British army after leaving prison under an arrangement tied to military service. During the German advance of 1940 he retreats toward Dunkirk with two other soldiers, Nettle and Mace. Robbie is wounded and increasingly feverish, but he is sustained by memories of Cecilia and by the hope of returning to her. She has become a nurse and separated herself from the Tallis family; the two maintained their commitment through letters and one brief meeting after his release. Crossing northern France, Robbie sees refugees, ruined towns, and the collapse of military order. The men finally reach the crowded evacuation area at Bray Dunes. Robbie hides the seriousness of his illness and lies down to rest while waiting for a chance to leave France.

Briony has abandoned her place at Cambridge and entered nurse training in London, partly following Cecilia's path and partly submitting herself to a discipline that leaves little room for her old certainty. Under Sister Drummond she learns demanding routines and cares for wounded soldiers arriving from France. Writing remains the means by which she examines the crime of her childhood. She learns that Lola is to marry Paul Marshall and attends their wedding, understanding that the marriage binds the victim to the man Briony now believes committed the assault. Briony then visits Cecilia, where Robbie is also staying. She acknowledges that her accusation was false and agrees to make a formal statement, contact the authorities, and name Marshall. Cecilia and Robbie remain angry but focused on the practical steps required to correct the record.

In 1999, Briony is an acclaimed novelist and has just learned that vascular dementia will progressively destroy her memory and language. She attends a family gathering at the old Tallis house and reflects on the manuscript she has revised throughout her life. The account of her wartime visit to Cecilia and Robbie was invented: she never apologized to them in person or secured a retraction. Robbie died of septicemia at Bray Dunes before he could be evacuated, and Cecilia died later in 1940 when a bomb caused flooding at Balham Underground station. Lola and Paul Marshall remained married, wealthy, and powerful; while they live, the legal risk prevents Briony from publishing a version that identifies them. Her completed novel gives Cecilia and Robbie a reunion and future that history denied them. Briony offers this imagined happiness as her final act of atonement, while doubting that a novelist who determines every outcome can also declare herself forgiven.

characters.description: Ilea's missing companion, carried into this volume as an unresolved personal concern.
characters.name: Kyrian

characters.description: Ilea's deceased investigator ally, remembered at the start of the volume as an unfinished personal loss. The circumstances of Eve's death remain unknown, as does the significance of her connection to the Golden Lily and the identity of whoever killed her.
characters.name: Eve

characters.description: An Azarinth Sentinel and Kin of Ash who has returned to Ravenhall after distant travels. Known publicly as Lilith, Ilea supports the city and its new combat-healer school while postponing her next class advancement to strengthen her broader skills and resistances.
characters.name: Ilea Spears

characters.description: A Ravenhall administrator and trusted confidante who knows Ilea's public identity. Claire coordinates the city's expanding projects, tracks regional developments, and advises Ilea as she approaches another class advancement.
characters.name: Claire

characters.description: Ilea's ally and an organizer of the Medic Sentinels. Trian helps oversee the young combat-healer program, assists with its practical training, and understands both Ilea's unusual progress and her decision to delay pursuing a third class.
characters.name: Trian

characters.description: A skeptical Medic Sentinel recruit displaced by violence in Varan. Scarred and wary of the school's wealth and loose structure, Nathan is nevertheless attracted to training that promises both healing ability and the strength to protect himself.
characters.name: Nathan

characters.description: A practical Medic Sentinel recruit who survived Ravenhall’s earlier disaster. Celeste welcomes the prospect of combining healing work with direct combat capability.
characters.name: Celeste

characters.description: A young farmer recruited by the Medic Sentinels. Luke trusts the new program more readily than some of his peers and is motivated by a straightforward wish to heal other people. His open confidence in the school contrasts with Nathan's initial suspicion.
characters.name: Luke

characters.description: A sentient enchanted dagger who spars with Ilea during a Medic Sentinel demonstration and serves as a combat-training asset for the school.
characters.name: Aki

characters.description: A member of the Medic Sentinel faculty who supports the independent combat-healer school.
characters.name: Orthon

characters.description: An enchanter developing an experimental teleportation gate with Christopher. Iana also examines Ilea's Taleen tungsten key, though both research projects remain unsafe and incomplete.
characters.name: Iana

characters.description: An enchanter working with Iana on an incomplete teleportation gate and the study of Ilea's complex Taleen tungsten key.
characters.name: Christopher

characters.description: A ranger who leads a four-person adventuring party preparing to enter the Caverns of Rot.
characters.name: Sean

characters.description: An ice mage traveling with Sean's four-person adventuring party in the Caverns of Rot.
characters.name: Sophia

characters.description: An investigator working for Ilea who reports a possible lead concerning Eve’s earlier identity.
characters.name: Dagon

characters.description: An investigator working for Ilea who helps trace a possible connection between Eve and a woman long presumed dead in Farport.
characters.name: Elise

characters.description: Riverwatch's governor, facing attacks on roads, caravans, and hunters. Alistair asks Ilea to identify the hostile force and assess its capabilities as the city prepares for the possibility of a larger assault.
characters.name: Alistair

characters.description: A formerly enslaved assassin captured while scouting near Riverwatch. Ilea removes the explosive teeth used to control him and heals him, after which Ario supplies information about the hostile camp and chooses to seek others still held in bondage.
characters.name: Ario

characters.description: A Riverwatch guard captain and Ilea's friend. During preparations for retaliation from Weinhold, Dale helps plan the city's defense and accepts a magical mark that lets Ilea locate him and receive a very short emergency message.
characters.name: Dale

characters.description: A level-285 astral mage and Shadow who duels Ilea outside Riverwatch. Rivka’s attacks grant Ilea Astral Magic Resistance, and she accepts an invitation to train at Ravenhall if she returns.
characters.name: Rivka

characters.description: A Medic Sentinel trainee taking part in the corps' supervised dungeon-survival program. Lorelai joins Nathan, Luke, and Celeste in field exercises designed to turn classroom training into independent healing and combat experience.
characters.name: Lorelai

characters.description: An Imperial wind mage caught in the aftermath of Odia's blood-and-curse ritual. Felicia shields surviving troops during the blast and helps carry the wounded toward treatment while cursed soldiers turn on the remaining army.
characters.name: Felicia

characters.description: An experienced poison user directing an investigation into the Order of Truth after Odia's catastrophic ritual. Helena receives prisoners and intelligence through her assassin Amara while assessing the wider purpose behind the attack.
characters.name: Helena

characters.description: An assassin and investigator serving Helena. Amara identifies a defecting Baralian officer, delivers him and an Order of Truth prisoner for questioning, and determines that victims of the Odia curse do not pass it to others.
characters.name: Amara

characters.description: A renowned level-362 pirate and sea mage assembled for a covert operation. Known only by his title at first, the Destroyer challenges Ilea with water powerful enough to dissolve her ash and launch multiple high-pressure attacks.
characters.name: The Destroyer

characters.description: A level-275 blood-magic specialist in fluid-looking golden armor who joins the covert operation against the Order of Truth's destructive rituals.
characters.name: Blood-and-gold mage

characters.description: A level-302 lightning mage, Golden Lily member, and Lys general who leads the strike mission investigating cities devastated by the Order of Truth's rituals.
characters.name: Lys general

characters.description: The sea mage previously introduced as the Destroyer reveals that his name is Hector. He uses massive water attacks and dangerous aquatic creatures during the mission investigating the Order of Truth's destructive, spatially distorted rituals.
characters.name: Hector

characters.description: A poor longtime resident of the city infiltrated by Ilea's strike team. Ivan confirms rumors of blood sacrifices and becomes Ilea's local contact, pointing her to a charitable healer within the Order of Truth.
characters.name: Ivan

characters.description: A charitable Order of Truth acolyte who quietly treats people unable to pay. Nicholas agrees to meet Ilea's strike team after she proves a local slaver is dead, then accepts evidence that senior members of his order are preparing a lethal ritual beneath the city.
characters.name: Nicholas

characters.description: An extremely powerful presence encountered in a crystal-tree sanctuary. It communicates mentally with Ilea, guides creatures toward awakening, and opened the fissure to offer endangered awakened residents a possible escape.
characters.name: Sanctuary being

characters.description: A blood-and-gold mage able to create independently acting copies of himself. Michael begins technical discussions with Endless Meadow about the open gate and the problem of moving Erendar's threatened survivors.
characters.name: Michael

characters.description: The ancient sanctuary guardian previously encountered by Ilea, now named Endless Meadow. A telepathic space mage, it protects 53 awakened survivors in Erendar and begins training Ilea while they seek a way to evacuate its dependents.
characters.name: Endless Meadow

characters.description: The first ant-like Erendar survivor selected to test Ilea's evacuation plan. Zarevika must endure both the gate crossing and Elos's lower mana while Ilea heals and carries her toward the mana-rich North.
characters.name: Zarevika

characters.description: Hallowfort's leader and a close friend of Ilea. Catelyn has been investigating corruption in the Descent and believed Ilea might have died there until Ilea returns seeking refuge for displaced awakened beings.
characters.name: Catelyn

characters.description: A hill-sized, four-mark ice being found among frozen astral remains in Erendar's mountains. It cannot communicate through ordinary speech, but recognizes Ilea's magical images of Endless Meadow, the gate, and the expected attack, then follows her toward the sanctuary.
characters.name: Ancient ice elemental

characters.description: A four-mark astral predator that descends when Endless Meadow begins closing the gate. Assessed by Ilea at roughly level 1,700, the first Daughter of Cephalon attacks the runic monolith and its ice elemental defender.
characters.name: First Daughter of Cephalon

recaps.ending: Ilea completes the evacuation of Erendar's 53 awakened survivors, delivering them to Hallowfort and securing Catelyn's protection for their four peoples. She then returns to help Endless Meadow close the realm gate. Ilea and the ancient ice elemental defend the closure monolith against two Daughters of Cephalon, and the resulting storm devastates the attacking spirits. Michael's copies die after documenting the event, leaving two notebooks with Ilea. The ice elemental remains in Erendar, while Ilea transports Endless Meadow to Elos in a reduced stone form. The gate disappears without residue. Hallowfort accepts Endless Meadow as an ally and gives it a mana-rich cavern between the settlement and the Descent. Ravenhall's Medic Sentinels and Taleen research continue, but Kyrian remains unreachable. Eve's murder, Helena's wider agenda, the Order of Truth's remaining plans, Baralia's war, the active Taleen production site, and Erendar's surviving dangers remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Back in Ravenhall, Ilea expands the Medic Sentinels, trains her resistances, saves Riverwatch from an invading slave-taking army, and becomes eligible for a third class. She chooses a Fae-and-Valkyrie path centered on space and creation flame, then joins Helena's elite mission against the Order of Truth's city-killing rituals. The mission stops several attacks but leaves a stable fissure to Erendar. There, Ilea meets Endless Meadow, guardian of 53 awakened survivors threatened by an eclipse and astral spirits. After months of training, she moves every refugee to Hallowfort. Ilea returns for the gate closure, battles the Daughters of Cephalon beside an ancient ice elemental, and carries the weakened Endless Meadow to Elos. Hallowfort accepts the refugees and their guardian, while Kyrian, Eve's murder, the Taleen gates, Baralia's war, and the larger ambitions of the Golden Lily and Order of Truth remain open.

recaps.text: Previously: Ilea Spears, also known publicly as Lilith, has become an Azarinth Sentinel and Kin of Ash whose healing, ash magic, and teleportation let her survive threats beyond most human fighters. She is closely tied to Ravenhall, where Claire and Trian support her projects and political position. Her influence now extends beyond personal adventuring into the city's development and an independent school for combat healers. Her northern allies include Catelyn and Hallowfort. Ilea's companion Kyrian remains missing. Eve, an investigator allied with Ilea, is dead, and neither her killer nor the full meaning of her connection to the Golden Lily has been established. These absences remain personal obligations rather than settled history. Ilea enters this volume with growing public influence, unusually broad combat experience, and unfinished debts to both companions.

Ilea returns to Ravenhall and tells Claire and Trian about her recent travels. Kyrian is alive but trapped somewhere that may require enchantment work to reach. Rather than rush toward a third class, Ilea chooses to build resistances and general skills. She publicly takes charge of afternoon instruction for the Medic Sentinels, revealing herself as Lilith to the recruits. Nathan, Celeste, and Luke endure early lightning, blood-corruption, and ash training under her healing. Aki demonstrates direct combat and affirms that he remains with the school by choice as a guardian and teacher. Outside the school, Ilea explores Karheim's gem golems and blighted ruins for rare resistances, expands paid arena training, and begins formal dancing lessons with Claire. Iana and Christopher's teleportation project is still unsafe, but their examination of Ilea's tungsten artifact suggests it is one of twelve intricate Taleen keys. Orthon also begins testing whether Ilea's regenerated bone can become durable Sentinel armor.

Teleportation experiments establish a connection but still transfer only pieces of Ilea, making her regeneration essential to the research. Seeking stronger training, she joins Sean, Sophia, Edgar, and Colt in the Caverns of Rot. After revealing her level and ash defenses, she protects the party through encounters with Rotten Abominations, gaining flesh, bone, and rot-related defenses. The dungeon's deeper aura forces the group to withdraw. Sophia concludes that relentless danger is not the life she wants and chooses to pursue ownership of an inn. Ilea returns alone, kills one level-621 Specter of Rot, and preserves the others as future opponents while deliberately stopping short of her next level threshold. Back in Ravenhall, larger arena sessions broaden her resistance work. Dagon and Elise find a possible lead concerning Eve's earlier life, but Claire interrupts with a request from Riverwatch: Governor Alistair needs Lilith to investigate attacks and disappearances around the city. Ilea leaves to assess the threat herself.

Near Riverwatch, Ilea captures Ario, an enslaved assassin controlled through explosive teeth. After freeing and healing him, she uses his information to find a camp holding captives for Lord Harkin of Weinhold. She kills the camp commander, frees the prisoners, and brings evidence to Riverwatch, while Ario leaves to liberate others still enslaved. Ilea gives Dale an emergency mark before returning to training. Soon an organized army surrounds Riverwatch, breaks a gate, and begins a full assault. Dale calls for help. Ilea arrives as Lilith, orders the attackers to withdraw and release their enslaved fighters, then takes the field when their commander refuses. She destroys the elite formation, routs the army, and kills the fleeing lord. Riverwatch survives, and Dale directs the handling of prisoners, freed people, fires, and the dead.
